# The Ink and wash theme

Designed 2026-10-17. A fifth theme, beside the default, the retro, the cosy and the swiss: the app as an ink wash painting. Cream paper, black ink, a single seal red, plenty of empty space; the only calm theme. Second of the three themes kept after the cosy (Swiss, then Ink and wash, then Metro signage), started from the swiss's flat pieces. Its identifier is `ink`.

Mock-up (screen of a zone): `docs/theme-tracks.html`, "Ink and wash" card.

## What is decided

All the lines of 2026-10-17, in the order of the list of `docs/THEMES.md`.

1. **The register**: cream paper, black ink, a single red, that of a seal, and plenty of empty space. A tile is a diluted ink stain (a wash) with irregular edges, without an outline; the group titles are spaced, followed by a brush stroke that tapers. Every stroke of the theme is drawn by the same brush (line 9). It is neither raised nor shadowed (the cosy), nor on a strict grid (the swiss), nor grainy, nor decorated with Asia (no ideogram, no bamboo).
   - **The red is for the seal**: the waiting mark, the ticked box, the page header's seal, the danger button, the interaction card's corner. The floating button stays in ink (mock-up).
   - The mock-up's last red bar of the chart is not held: the core's drawing does not tell the theme which bar is today.
2. **What it draws itself**: everything, dialogs and date and time selectors included, starting from the swiss's flat pieces (same cut into files), their shapes taken again.
3. **The font**: Literata (SIL Open Font License 1.1, without a reserved name), kept on the bench 2026-10-17 against EB Garamond, whose small lowercases read less well; copied into `third_party/literata/`, a script `scripts/make_literata_fonts.py` draws from it three fixed weights: 400 the text and 600 the names and labels, at a text's optical size (12), 700 the titles at a title's (36); from its italic, copied beside, 400 and 600 at a text's size, for the italic of a read text. Shippori Mincho, the mock-up's, is set aside: it lacks `≤ ≥ ≠ ≈ Š Ž Ÿ ƒ ‰` and the narrow no-break space, and one weight weighs 8.7 MB (measured 2026-10-17). Literata covers Windows-1252, the arrows and `≤ ≥ ≠ ≈ − ×`; it only lacks the narrow space (U+202F), which the script adds like `make_archivo_fonts.py`. `✓ ✗` stay with Android's fallback, as in the swiss.
4. **The palettes** (OKLCH, lightness · saturation · hue; contrast aimed at 4.5, held at each 15° shift by `InkPaletteTest`); their numbers in `palettes.json`, set on the bench (`themes/ink/bench/palettes.html`, "Ink and wash · palettes"):
   - light: paper `#f3eee2` (0.95 · 0.017 · 88), ink `#1d1c1a` (0.227 ; 14.7), secondary at lightness 0.45 (6.4 on the paper, 4.8 on the rail, darker than the mock-up's `#6d6860`, which only held 3.9 on a wash), red at 0.514 · 0.159 (5.3 on the paper, 4.57 at the worst of the shifts), the paper on the red;
   - dark, light ink on a night paper, where nothing lights up (seen again 2026-10-17 on the phone, where light washes and bright colour stains made a neon effect): paper `#23211e` (0.25), ink `#e9e3d5` (0.917 ; 12.6), secondary at 0.74 (7.0), red less bright at 0.66 · 0.12 (4.9);
   - the washes, the share of an ink laid on the paper, that of the washes (`wash_lightness`): the ink itself in light, an ink darker than the paper in dark (0.10), the ink that soaks in: a tile's core 8.5% in light and 45% in dark, a card 7% and 38% (darkened by one notch 2026-10-17, when the wash began to go out at its edge), a rail (and a disabled button) 14% and 55%; no secondary text falls under 4.5 there;
   - the solids (primary button, floating button, chosen day, switch on): the full ink in light, the paper written on it; in dark, a grey of light ink washed out at 26% (`#57534e`), the light ink written on it (6.0); the toasts and the selection bar the same (88% in light); pressed, a solid loses 10% of its ink;
   - the stain of an icon's colour, 45% opacity in its core in light, 22% in dark, where a bright colour shines;
   - the red is only written on the danger button, on the paper: the mock-up chart's red figure goes to ink;
   - the hue turns the red and the paper's warmth, the ink following the paper's hue; states and tags kept; the tags at lightness 0.60 · 0.13 in light (3.2 at the worst on the paper, a mark, not a text), 0.72 · 0.12 in dark, drawn as small wash stains.
5. **The geometry**: `UI.Space` XS 4, S 8, M 16, L 24, XL 32, `EDGE` 16, the swiss's; more empty space than it between the grid's rows. Square cells, 16 dp between two columns, 20 between two rows, left empty by the grid; 14 × 8 dp inside a tile (mock-up). The finger target at 48 dp, the drawing able to be smaller. `drawingUnit` 1.
6. **The size**: Android's text size followed; the step (0 to 3) enlarges everything by ×1, ×1.12, ×1.25 and ×1.4, like the swiss, except the spacings, the edge margin and the grid's gaps, fixed in dp. The page title at 30 sp, going to the next line cut at the syllables.
7. **The components**:
   - frames: the tile, a wash with irregular edges, its texture cut to this shape and fading with the wash; the wash spills out of the tile by half the grid's spacings and goes out at its edge in each direction, dense on half the way (seen on the phone 2026-10-17: contained in the tile and computed to the farthest corner, it was cut straight at its edge); a single shape, stretched to each tile (the theme does not know which one it draws, and adding it to the contract to vary the shapes is not worth its cost); the card (variable, routine, line of a list), a pale but full wash, so that no pattern passes under a text, its edge undulating a little and fading out over 6 dp (seen on the phone 2026-10-17: as a neat pebble, it had nothing of an ink); the dialog and the floating window, full paper under a brush stroke on top; the user's bubble, an ink wash pushed right, the AI without a bubble, its text on the paper; the interaction card, a wash and a small red seal at the corner;
   - what is round (the floating button, a full or pressed icon button, the box, the switch's thumb, the slider, the state pill, the calendar's day) is a hand-painted disc, never a compass circle: round, a little oval and a little uneven, with a light tremble (`BlobShape`), that of a button drawn from its icon; a stain with marked lobes, tried first, was ugly;
   - buttons: primary, a brush touch full of ink, the paper's label; secondary, a brush outline; tertiary and neutral, the label alone underlined by a thin stroke; danger, red outline and label; disabled, a pale wash, label in secondary ink; on, full of ink; icon-only, the icon without a frame in 48 dp; the floating button, an ink pebble of 56 dp, the paper's icon;
   - input: the field, a thin brush stroke under the text, thicker at focus, the label above in secondary ink; the selection, the same field and a chevron, its menu a panel like the dialog; the box, a circle drawn with the brush, ticked the same circle holding a small round red seal (a square in the circle's place changed shape from one state to the other), this circle drawn by hand like everything round; the switch, a drawn pebble, on filled with ink; yes / no, the chosen in a full wash; the slider, a drop of ink on a stroke; the gauge, a brush stroke that tapers (mock-up) on a pale wash rail; the hue band in saturated colours; the tabs, the chosen underlined by a brush stroke;
   - marks: the tag, a small gouache stain of its colour before its text; the separator, a stroke that tapers; the handle, two short strokes; the waiting mark, a round red seal and a "!", a hand-painted disc like what is round, the square seal (the initial of the app's mark) with sides that tremble a little (`HandShape`); the timer mark, a circle drawn in one gesture (ensō); the coloured icon, in ink on a gouache stain of its colour (opaque, matte, in a solid, a hand-painted disc like what is round, its own shape for the icon), the same place without colour (seen on the phone 2026-10-17: a round stain going out from a bright core read as a light, and a transparent colour cannot brighten the night paper); the textures, slightly irregular brush patterns, in a very pale wash, on the tile and over the whole background of a textured page (`PageGround`);
   - waiting: the loading, the ensō tracing itself; the AI thinking, three drops that spread then pale one after the other;
   - messages: the toast and the snackbar, a dark wash at the bottom, the paper's text, the action underlined;
   - date and time: in the dialog's frame; the chosen day, a drop of full ink, today an open brush circle; the time, two counters like the swiss, − and + with the brush, without a dial;
   - page header and mark: the title centred and spaced, a red seal carrying its initial to its right (mock-up), the page's icon on its colour stain above; the app's mark, the icon's monochrome layer in ink, without the night blue;
   - the bar of a selected text: a dark wash, its words of the paper, the touched word underlined.
8. **The touch and the movement**: slow and soft, the opposite of the swiss's clean cut. The pressed element darkens by one wash notch, without a ripple; an appearance is a 220 ms fade that slows at the end, a closing a 150 ms fade; the lifted element darkens and shifts 4 dp, without a shadow. Animations cut in Android: everything instantaneous.
9. **The icons**: Lucide (`LUCIDE`), redrawn by the theme with the brush. The theme reads each icon's strokes (the vector file read as a list of strokes, `ImageVector.vectorResource`) and redraws them as a series of discs whose size follows the brush. The reading of the strokes is a brick of the core (`core/icons`), so that a future theme redraws Lucide its own way; the gesture is the theme's. The same brush draws all the theme's strokes (line 7). Its settings, chosen 2026-10-17 at the brush bench (`themes/ink/bench/brush.html`, "Ink and wash · brush" of `./run themes`), which draws like the theme:
   - thickness 1.3 (in units of Lucide's grid of 24);
   - brush direction 0.45: held at a slant, a stroke that rises gently to the right is the thinnest, up to 55% × 0.45 thinner than a crosswise stroke;
   - pressure at the elbows 1: the stroke thickens up to 60% in a quarter-turn bend;
   - landing 0.45: the stroke starts 60% × 0.45 thicker, back to its width in a third of its length (1.2 at most);
   - sway 0.3: a single slow swelling over the whole length, never an undulation;
   - taper 0.5: the end of the stroke lifts to a point, up to 6% of its width, over half its length at most (0.6 + 3.4 × 0.5);
   - the widths smoothed along the stroke; a closed stroke (a circle) without landing nor point;
   - wet edge: a half-transparent edge around a core at 72% of the width; no dry brush;
   - the gesture fixed per icon (the same icon always drawn the same), computed once per size and kept.
10. **The charts**: drawn by the theme (`InkDrawing`, started from `SwissDrawing`). A bar is a full wash that holds exactly its value, its top corners soft and a little uneven (with the brush, a wide bar became a drop that spilled past its value at the top and tapered at the bottom, seen on the phone 2026-10-17), the surfaces in transparent washes, the goal dotted, the axes in a thin stroke; the colours the user gives to the series kept, in wash.
11. **The edit mode of the grid**: a cell, a circle of a very pale wash; the chosen tile, the lifted tile of line 8.
12. **The sound register**: muffled, a brush on the paper, a turned page, a light wood; to look for in the soft impact sounds and the "drops" of Kenney. Chosen by ear: `sounds-choice.json`.
13. **The texts**: name "Ink and wash"; tagline "Like an ink wash painting: cream paper, black ink and a single seal red, plenty of empty space". No palette name.

## What is coded

`themes/ink/`: the palette (`InkPalette`, its numbers in `palettes.json`, set on the bench), the sizes and the font by step (`InkSize`), the brush (`InkBrush`), the pressed element, the fade, the lifted element, the wash's shape, the brushed icon and the seal (`InkPieces`), the charts (`InkDrawing`), each contract component (`InkTheme`), the textures' cells (`textures/`, touches of the same brush in full shapes). The reading of an icon's strokes is a brick of the core, `core/icons/IconStrokes`. `InkPaletteTest` holds the two palettes' contrasts at each 15° shift, on the paper and on the washes. Chosen in Settings › Interface, under the name "Ink and wash".

What the code made precise among the decisions:
- An icon, with sharp corners, is stamped as discs once per icon and per size into a mask kept in memory, then tinted; a smooth stroke (hairline, underline, circle, pebble, ensō) is a single outline around its widths, redrawn at no cost. An icon's full parts (about ten Lucide icons) are filled.
- A window closes at once, as in the other themes: the floating window, common to all, leaves the screen as soon as it is closed, and an exit fade would ask the core to keep it for the fade's time.
- A tile's irregular shape is the same for all, stretched to its size.
- An icon-only tile has no wash at rest: its icon alone on the paper, the icon's colour as a stain around it.
- The textures' tones: the swiss's, brought in light to the cosy's (×0.4), too marked on the phone.

## What stays open

- The pass of `docs/THEMES.md`, on what changed 2026-10-17 after the first: a tile's wash that spills and goes out at its edge, its texture faded with it, the card in wash with a faded edge (steps in the fade?), the gouache under the icons and the tags, the hand-painted rounds (buttons, box, seals), the cost of opening a zone with textured tiles; the cost of the brushed icons (a page full of icons at its first opening) and the icons that clog.
- A tile's name stays centred by the core (`UI.TileHeader`), as the mock-up wants it.
- The textures' tones, to set on the textures bench (`./run themes`).
- Once the redrawn Lucide is held on the phone (cost, icons that clog): the third way of line 9 of the recipe, `docs/THEMES.md`.
